name: Caro-Kann Defense, Advance Variation
white_ideas: Patient development, as you have space advantage and center is closed. Start Nf6. Take dxc5 if they push c5
black_ideas:
Option 1: Bf5 before it gets trapped, then lock down with e6. Challenge with c5 when it's supported, which may be right away. Use moves like Bg4 (attacking knight on f3), e6, Ne7 to f5, and Qb6 to attack d4
Option 2: immediate c5. Arguably easier to play

Option 2: If white does b4, immediately do a5. Don't let that queenside pawn chain exist. If they do c3, take anyway and attack the next pawn with b6. Can also play Nd7, and if they pin w/ light bishop, bring in other horse to unpin (slow)
white_risks: Thinking you can pin e pawn with Bg5. Black just moves the queen Qb5 to threaten b pawn
black_risks: If you c5 and they dxc5, don't try to get the bishop out. Play e6, accept that it's trapped

name: Caro-Kann Defense, Exchange Variation
black_ideas: Pretty normal game. If they do c4, you play Nf3

name: Caro-Kann Defense, General
white_ideas: Take the center and establish and dark-squared pawn chain.
black_ideas:
Central idea: get a nice solid position and try to destroy White's central dark square pawn chain

Asymmetric attack on the center. Establish a well-supported pawn in the center of the board. Black tries to destroy this pawn chain by attacking d4 or sometimes even c3.

Accept loss of light bishop, as our pawn chain will be light squared. Good to trade it for knight on f3 if possible to weaken d4

name: Caro-Kann Defense, Standard, Unorthodox Replies
white_ideas: Fall the knight back if Bf5. Then develop
black_ideas: Bf5 attacking knight. Bg6 if they attack with knight, e6 if queen

name: Italian Game, General
white_ideas: Pressure f7 pawn. Castle fast. White may attempt fried liver attack or scholar's mate
black_ideas: No immediate pressure. Giuoco piano for slow, two knights for fast
black_risks: White may attempt fried liver attack, i.e. Ng5 for a double attack on f7. Can counter by going Giuoco piano, keeping queen pointed at g5 and buying time to castle. If I go two knights, I need to know a line to stay even

name: Italian Game, Two Knights Defense
white_ideas: d3 to defend the pawn, NOT Nc3. Or gambit with d4, then push e5 for control or castle for safety
black_ideas: If d4: Take the pawn exd4, then if they push e5, do d5 intermezzo then move your knight Ne5. It's fine if they en passant, just take with bishop
white_risks: 4. Nc3. Allows Nxe5, as recapturing with knight allows a center fork
black_risks: If they do fried liver attack 4.Ng5, MUST play this line: 4...d5 5.exd5 Na6 6.Bb5+ c6 7. dxc6 bxc6. then the threat is gone. If they 5.Nxf7 after d5, do 5...Kxf7 6.exd5 b5. 3 options: if they take knight, take bishop. if they take pawn, take pawn with queen. if they retreat bishop, take pawn with queen if safe, else attack bishop with knight

name: King Pawn Game, General
black_risks: White going for immediate f7 checkmate. Defend 2.Qa4 with Nc3, 2.Bc3 or 2.Qf3 with Nf6 (blocks Qa5 moves),

name: Queen Pawn Game, Symmetrical Variation, Pseudo-Catalan
Scandinavian Defense, Mieses-Kotroc Variation
white_ideas: Take the trade, chase the queen with Nc3. Then Nf3 is good, or Bc4+d4, or maybe d4+Bc2. Bc4+d2 seems less sharp
black_ideas: Put pressure on d4 if they don't defend it
white_risks: Not knowing how to defend against Queen on d file, b file, concentrated attack with bishop. Panicking when Qxb5

name: Spanish Game, General
white_ideas: Eventually play c3 and d4 to build a pawn majority in the centre. Castle fast. Threaten e pawn by removing its defender, forcing defensive play
black_ideas:
Ignore the bishop with Nf6
Kick it with Morphy defense, a6. If they trade, know the tactic to win back the e pawn (Qe4 after Nxe5)
white_risks: Thinking you can win a pawn by trading the bishop for knight: Bxc3 dxc3 Nxe5. In reality, black plays Qe4 and wins the pawn back
black_risks:
Doubled pawns
Taking back bishop with bxc3 instead of dxc3. The former creates 3 pawn islands rather than 2. The former also makes it harder to win back the e pawn, though can use Qe7 then d6 to attack knight
